definitions.explanation: Having the same quality, quantity, or condition throughout. No variation or unevenness.
A single fixed price for all items or services. Commonly seen in shops where everything costs the same amount.

examples.japanese: {品質|ひんしつ}を{均一|きんいつ}に{保|たも}つ。
{温度|おんど}が{均一|きんいつ}になるようによくかき{混|ま}ぜる。
examples.english: Stir well so that the temperature becomes uniform.

examples.japanese: {生地|きじ}の{厚|あつ}さを{均一|きんいつ}にするのが{難|むずか}しい。
examples.english: It's hard to make the dough thickness uniform.

examples.japanese: {百円|ひゃくえん}{均一|きんいつ}の{店|みせ}で{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought it at a 100-yen flat-rate shop.

examples.japanese: バスの{運賃|うんちん}は{均一|きんいつ}{料金|りょうきん}だ。
examples.english: The bus fare is a flat rate.

examples.japanese: {千円|せんえん}{均一|きんいつ}セールを{開催|かいさい}している。
examples.english: They are holding a 1,000-yen flat-rate sale.

notes:
USAGE:
Sense 2 is particularly common in daily life. {百円|ひゃくえん}{均一|きんいつ} (100-yen shops) are ubiquitous in Japan — the word is often shortened to {百均|ひゃっきん} in casual speech. Many city buses also charge {均一|きんいつ}{料金|りょうきん} (flat-rate fares).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {百円|ひゃくえん}{均一|きんいつ}: 100-yen flat rate (100-yen shop)
- {均一|きんいつ}{料金|りょうきん}: flat-rate charge
- {均一|きんいつ}に{保|たも}つ: to keep uniform
- {品質|ひんしつ}が{均一|きんいつ}: uniform quality
